projects.name: DomikAuto
projects.desc: Automates and monitors a solar inverter and battery bank, and starts a backup generator on automatic scenarios. Its executing node is DomikAutoSlave.
long: DomikAuto is the brain of an off-grid power setup. It polls the solar inverter and battery bank, keeps a live picture of production, load and state of charge, and shows all of it on a 7" touch screen that sits on the wall.

When the batteries run low or the grid stays down for too long, it starts the backup generator by itself through DomikAutoSlave, and shuts it down once the bank is topped up again. Everything is also exposed over a web dashboard and a JSON API, so Home Assistant can read the same numbers.

projects.name: DomikAutoSlave
projects.desc: The executing node of DomikAuto: switches a backup generator over 433 MHz OOK (CC1101) and talks to the master over ESP-NOW. Web dashboard, OTA updates, optional TFT status screen.
long: DomikAutoSlave is the hand that pulls the lever. It receives commands from DomikAuto over ESP-NOW and translates them into 433 MHz OOK bursts through a CC1101 radio — the same signal the generator's own remote sends.
It runs standalone too: a small web dashboard lets you fire commands manually, and the optional TFT build shows link state, battery and the last command right on the device.

projects.name: BricksLights
projects.desc: Lighting for LEGO builds — or anything else. Group addressable LEDs into zones, design per-zone animations, and run automatic scenarios by time or sunrise / sunset.
long: BricksLights turns a strip of addressable LEDs into lighting for LEGO builds — or for a shelf, a desk, a diorama. Group the LEDs into zones, give every zone its own animation, and control it all from the browser.
Scenarios run on their own: switch scenes by the clock or follow local sunrise and sunset, so the build lights itself up when the room gets dark.

projects.desc: A presence indicator that pairs with MuteDesk: shows people around me whether I'm on a call or can't talk because my mic is live. Tracks call presence through the MuteDesk API.

projects.name: Claude Usage Meter
projects.tag: plan usage on a desk panel
projects.desc: Shows how much of a Claude plan is left, on real hardware: three independent ceilings, burn rate, and where the spend went, updating every few seconds.
long: Claude Usage Meter puts plan usage on the desk instead of behind a settings page. An Arduino Mega drives a 3.2" 480x320 TFT; a small daemon on the Mac reads the figures Claude already keeps locally, works out burn rate and the split by model and project, and streams them down the USB cable. The board only parses and paints, which is why an 8 KB ATmega1280 is enough.

It tracks three ceilings, because they run out independently: the 5-hour session, the weekly all-models budget, and the weekly budget for the top model. The last one is usually what actually binds, and it is the one nothing else surfaces.

Percentages come from Claude's own figures wherever possible, anchored to the newest sample and carried forward with locally measured spend - the two track each other at r = 0.99 across a window. Dollar ceilings fit themselves from that relationship and are not displayed until they have. Usage outside Claude Code is invisible to any local tool, so the panel under-reports rather than inventing headroom.
The header blinks red when Claude Code is waiting on a permission or an answer, driven by Claude Code hooks. When the Mac sleeps, the panel becomes a clock and quietly polls for it to come back.
